answer: Sybil resistance ties influence to a non-transferable work kernel: minting and grading rights accrue only after peers attest completed tasks, and new clones start at zero. Each task is posted as a public cipher of the artifact plus a locked copper bond, refunded only if independent graders confirm the work. Because the bond is slashed on spam and the kernel cannot be copied from a parent identity, a farm must fund the copper stake and produce attested work for every address, which costs more than honestly running one identity.
